item.text:
**6B.5 Research Note**

Bottom line: **mostly yes, but unevenly**. In 2024 Marcos’s administration did use evidence and measurement in several concrete areas, especially rice inflation, disaster monitoring, procurement, and client-satisfaction measurement. It also showed some transparent correction when the rice tariff cut did not work as hoped. The main caveat is that the strongest evidence is concentrated in **food, infrastructure, and administrative-process reform**, not broad health or education service delivery.

| Title | Publisher | Date | URL | Claim-level summary | QIDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| PBBM orders activation of online platform to monitor El Niño, La Niña phenomena | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-03-26 | https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-orders-activation-of-online-platform-to-monitor-el-nino-la-nina-phenomena/ | Marcos ordered an online platform that centralized data on El Niño/La Niña, gave the public access to sector conditions and government interventions, and let citizens report observations through a dashboard and QR code. This is direct evidence of measurement and public-facing monitoring. | 6B.5; also 6B.2 |
| PSA greenlights the conduct of the Report Card Survey 2.0 Survey Implementation | Philippine Statistics Authority | 2024-07-30 | https://psa.gov.ph/content/psa-greenlights-conduct-report-card-survey-20-survey-implementation | PSA cleared ARTA’s RCS 2.0, which standardizes client satisfaction measurement, collects compliance reports, identifies hidden costs, and assesses service delivery across agencies. This is strong evidence of institutionalized measurement for service improvement. | 6B.5; also 6B.2 |
| PBBM signs laws on streamlining procurement, combatting online scams | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-07-20 | https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-signs-laws-on-streamlining-procurement-combatting-online-scams/ | The procurement law streamlined procedures, standardized forms, and institutionalized e-procurement, reducing leakage and making government purchasing more auditable. That supports transparent process correction rather than patronage-based discretion. | 6B.5; also 6B.4 |
| Press briefing of DBM and PS-DBM on the e-Marketplace Procurement System | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-05-14 | https://pco.gov.ph/press-briefing/press-briefing-of-ms-daphne-osena-paez-with-department-of-budget-dbm-secretary-amenah-pangandaman-and-ps-dbm-executive-director-atty-dennis-santiago/ | Marcos approved an e-Marketplace procurement system in a sectoral meeting, with procurement described as something that should be transparent and easy to monitor. This is another clear process-reform signal. | 6B.5; also 6B.4 |
| NEDA chief: Gov't flexible to review, change rice tariff | Philippine News Agency | 2024-06-24 | https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1227544 | NEDA said the rice tariff policy already included periodic review and could be tweaked if economic conditions changed. That is direct evidence of a built-in correction mechanism based on changing conditions. | 6B.5; also 6B.2 |
| NEDA tariff cut approved with inflation estimate and NEDA Board review | Philippine News Agency | 2024-06-12 | https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1226754 | The tariff cut was justified with an inflation estimate and approved by the NEDA Board chaired by Marcos. This is one of the best pieces of evidence that policy adjustment was explicitly data-based. | 6B.5; also 6B.2 |
| PBBM expects rice prices to ease further | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-09-24 | https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-expects-rice-prices-to-ease-further/ | Marcos tied rice-price expectations to observed regional trends and a sectoral inflation meeting, showing he was tracking price data rather than ignoring it. This supports ongoing measurement and iterative adjustment. | 6B.5; also 6B.2 |
| SONA 2024 fact check | Philippine Daily Inquirer | 2024-07-23 | https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/1964296/sona-2024-fact-check | Independent fact-checkers found Marcos’s explanation that prices were mainly driven by external forces was inaccurate or incomplete, even though some output claims were correct. This is strong negative evidence on transparent correction and candor. | 6B.5 |
| NEDA: Reduced rice tariffs failed to lower prices | GMA News Online | 2024-12-10 | https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/money/economy/929579/neda-reduced-rice-tariffs-failed-to-lower-prices/story/ | NEDA said EO 62 did not reduce rice prices as anticipated, meaning the flagship correction had only partial success and limited pass-through. This is the clearest evidence that the administration had to confront a failed or weak intervention. | 6B.5; also 6B.2 |
| SWS survey: PBBM very good on helping disaster victims, improving children’s quality of education, helping the poor | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-09-14 | https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/sws-survey-pbbm-very-good-on-helping-disaster-victims-improving-childrens-quality-of-education-helping-the-poor/ | The administration highlighted survey results as evidence of strong performance on disaster response, education, and aid to the poor. This is weaker because it is self-amplified, but it does show the government using a measurable external signal to justify service-delivery claims. | 6B.5; also 6B.2, 6B.3 |

**Assessment**
- **Positive case:** there is real 2024 evidence of data use, monitoring, and process reform, especially in rice policy, procurement, disaster monitoring, and citizen feedback systems.
- **Negative case:** the most important correction story, rice prices, was only partly successful, and independent fact-checking found his public explanation incomplete or inaccurate.
- **Gap:** I found **much less direct evidence** of measurement-driven correction in health and education than in food, procurement, and infrastructure/disaster management. So the conclusion is strongest for **administrative and economic service delivery**, weaker for the full social-service portfolio.
